facts.statement: The genus Kritosaurus was described by Brown in 1910.
facts.quote: authority: Brown, 1910

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Kritosaurus is Kritosaurus navajovius.
facts.quote: type_species: Kritosaurus navajovius

facts.statement: Kritosaurus is an incompletely known genus of duck-billed dinosaur.
facts.quote: Kritosaurus is an incompletely known genus of hadrosaurid (duck-billed) dinosaur.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus lived approximately 74.5 to 66 million years ago during the Late Cretaceous in North America.
facts.quote: It lived about 74.5-66 million years ago, in the Late Cretaceous of North America.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown discovered the type specimen of Kritosaurus in 1904 near the Ojo Alamo Formation in San Juan County, New Mexico.
facts.quote: In 1904, Barnum Brown discovered the type specimen (AMNH 5799) of Kritosaurus near the Ojo Alamo Formation, San Juan County, New Mexico, United States, while following up on a previous expedition.

facts.statement: By 1916, the age of the Kritosaurus fossils was established as the late Campanian-age De-na-zin Member of the Kirtland Formation.
facts.quote: by 1916 was able to establish it as from what is now known as the late Campanian-age De-na-zin Member of the Kirtland Formation.

facts.statement: Barnum Brown initially intended to name the dinosaur Nectosaurus but found the name was already in use.
facts.quote: He initially wanted to name it Nectosaurus, but found out that this name was already in use

facts.statement: Barnum Brown synonymized the genus Gryposaurus with Kritosaurus, a classification supported by Charles Gilmore.
facts.quote: He also synonymized Gryposaurus with Kritosaurus, a move supported by Charles Gilmore.

facts.statement: Lull and Wright assigned the species Hadrosaurus breviceps to Kritosaurus, but this classification is no longer accepted.
facts.quote: The poorly known species Hadrosaurus breviceps (Marsh, 1889), known from a dentary from the Campanian-age Judith River Formation of Montana, was also assigned to Kritosaurus by Lull and Wright, but this is no longer accepted.

facts.statement: In 1984, José Bonaparte and colleagues named the species Kritosaurus australis based on fossils from Patagonia, Argentina.
facts.quote: In 1984, Argentine paleontologist José Bonaparte and colleagues named Kritosaurus australis for hadrosaur bones from the late Campanian-early Maastrichtian Los Alamitos Formation of Rio Negro, Patagonia, Argentina.

facts.statement: Further analysis proved that Kritosaurus australis belongs to a new genus, which was named Huallasaurus by Rozadilla et al. in 2022.
facts.quote: In 2010, this species was thought to be a synonym of Secernosaurus koerneri. Further analysis proved the bones to belong to a new genus. Thus, Huallasaurus was named by Rozadilla et al. (2022).

facts.statement: In 1990, Jack Horner and David B. Weishampel separated the genus Gryposaurus from Kritosaurus due to uncertainty regarding Gryposaurus material.
facts.quote: In 1990, Jack Horner and David B. Weishampel once again separated Gryposaurus, citing the uncertainty associated with the latter's partial skull.

facts.statement: Adrian Hunt and Spencer G. Lucas named the species Anasazisaurus horneri in 1993.
facts.quote: Adrian Hunt and Spencer G. Lucas, American paleontologists, named Anasazisaurus horneri in 1993.

facts.statement: The name Anasazisaurus is derived from the Anasazi people and the Greek word for lizard.
facts.quote: The name was derived from the Anasazi, an ancient Native American people, and the Greek word sauros ("lizard").

facts.statement: The holotype skull of Anasazisaurus horneri was collected in the late 1970s in San Juan County and is housed at BYU as specimen BYU 12950.
facts.quote: The holotype skull (and only known specimen) was collected in the late 1970s by a Brigham Young University field party working in San Juan County, and is housed at BYU as BYU 12950.

facts.statement: In 2002, a partial left maxilla from Big Bend National Park was assigned to Kritosaurus navajovius.
facts.quote: In 2002, specimen TxVP 41917–1, a partial left maxilla recovered from Bruja Canyon in Big Bend National Park, was assigned to Kritosaurus, as cf. K. navajovius.

facts.statement: In 2023, Prieto-Márquez and Wagner named the new taxon Malefica based on a specimen previously assigned to Kritosaurus.
facts.quote: Twenty years later, it was discovered to contain a number of useful diagnostic traits that allow it to be described as a new taxon, and thus Malefica was named by Prieto-Márquez and Wagner (2023).

facts.statement: It is debated whether Kritosaurus is a valid genus, as Hunt and Lucas judged it a nomen dubium due to a lack of diagnostic features.
facts.quote: Horner originally assigned the Anasazisaurus skull to Kritosaurus navajovius, but Hunt and Lucas could not find any diagnostic features in the limited material of Kritosaurus and judged the genus to be a nomen dubium.

facts.statement: Some authors, including Thomas E. Williamson, defend the interpretation that Anasazisaurus and Kritosaurus are distinct genera.
facts.quote: Not all authors have agreed with this, Thomas E. Williamson in particular defending Horner's original interpretation, and several subsequent studies recognized both distinct genera.

facts.statement: A 2013 study by Albert Prieto-Márquez found the type specimens of Kritosaurus and Anasazisaurus indistinguishable when comparing overlapping elements.
facts.quote: A comprehensive study of known Kritosaurus material published by Albert Prieto-Márquez in 2013 upheld the status of Naashoibitosaurus as a distinct genus, but found that the type specimens of Kritosaurus and Anasazisaurus were indistinguishable when comparing overlapping elements

facts.statement: Albert Prieto-Márquez regarded Anasazisaurus as a synonym of Kritosaurus but retained it as the species K. horneri.
facts.quote: Prieto-Márquez therefore regarded Anasazisaurus as a synonym of Kritosaurus, but retained it as the distinct species K. horneri.

facts.statement: A partial skeleton from the Sabinas Basin in Mexico was described as Kritosaurus sp. but later considered an indeterminate saurolophine.
facts.quote: A partial skeleton from the Sabinas Basin in Mexico was described as Kritosaurus sp. by Jim Kirkland and colleagues, but considered an indeterminate saurolophine by Prieto-Márquez (2013).

facts.statement: The partial skeleton from the Sabinas Basin is approximately 11 meters (36 ft) long and about 20% larger than other known specimens.
facts.quote: This skeleton is about 20% larger than other known specimens, around 11 meters [36 ft] long, and with a distinctively curved ischium

facts.statement: Kritosaurus fossils have been found in the Olmos Formation in Mexico.
facts.quote: Kritosaurus fossils have also been unearthed in the Olmos Formation in Mexico.

facts.statement: The type specimen of Kritosaurus navajovius consists of a partial skull, lower jaws, and associated postcranial remains.
facts.quote: The type specimen of Kritosaurus navajovius is only represented by a partial skull and lower jaws, and associated postcranial remains.

facts.statement: The remains indicate that Kritosaurus reached a body length of 9 meters and a mass of 4 metric tons.
facts.quote: However, these remains alone indicate a large body size, reaching 9 m in length and 4 MT in body mass.

facts.statement: The crest is described as a tab of bone rising between and above the eyes and folding back under itself.
facts.quote: Based on the skull originally referred to Anasazisaurus, the form of the complete crest is that of a tab or flange of bone, from the nasals, that rises between and above the eyes and folds back under itself.

facts.statement: Diagnostic features include a predentary without tooth-like crenulations, a sharp downward bend in the lower jaws, and a heavy, rectangular maxilla.
facts.quote: Potential diagnostic characteristics of Kritosaurus include a predentary (lower beak) without tooth-like crenulations, a sharp downward bend to the lower jaws near the beak, and a heavy, somewhat rectangular maxilla (upper tooth-bearing bone).

facts.statement: Kritosaurus was classified as a hadrosaurine hadrosaurid, characterized as a flat-headed or solid-crested duckbill.
facts.quote: Kritosaurus was a hadrosaurine hadrosaurid, a flat-headed or solid-crested duckbill.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus navajovius is the closest relative of Anasazisaurus horneri, and both belong to the clade Kritosaurini within Saurolophinae.
facts.quote: The closest relative of Kritosaurus navajovius is Anasazisaurus horneri (or Kritosaurus horneri), which, together with close relatives such as Gryposaurus and Secernosaurus, form a clade called the Kritosaurini within the larger clade Saurolophinae.

facts.statement: The habitat of Kritosaurus was interpreted as river floodplains that formed after the retreat of the Western Interior Seaway.
facts.quote: The Kirtland Formation is interpreted as river floodplains appearing after a retreat of the Western Interior Seaway.

facts.statement: Conifers were the dominant plants in the environment, and chasmosaurine horned dinosaurs were more common than hadrosaurids.
facts.quote: Conifers were the dominant plants, and chasmosaurine horned dinosaurs appear to have been more common than hadrosaurids.

facts.statement: There is a debate regarding the age of the Kritosaurus holotype because the Ojo Alamo Formation is divided by an unconformity into older Campanian and younger Maastrichtian members.
facts.quote: However, not all of the paleontological community agrees with the age of the Kritosaurus holotype unearthed by Barnum Brown. This is due to the unconformity that divides the Ojo Alamo Formation into two parts; the older Naashoibito member, which overlies the Campanian era Kirtland Formation, and the younger Kimbeto member.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the nasal crest may have been used for social functions like identifying sex, species, or social ranking.
facts.quote: The nasal crest of Kritosaurus, whatever its true form, may have been used for a variety of social functions, such as identification of sexes or species and social ranking.

facts.statement: It is hypothesized that inflatable air sacs flanked the crest for visual and auditory signaling.
facts.quote: There may have been inflatable air sacs flanking it for both visual and auditory signaling.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus was a large bipedal or quadrupedal herbivore that used a grinding motion analogous to chewing.
facts.quote: As a hadrosaurid, Kritosaurus would have been a large bipedal/quadrupedal herbivore, eating plants with a sophisticated skull that permitted a grinding motion analogous to chewing.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus had continuously replacing teeth packed into dental batteries containing hundreds of teeth, with only a few in use at any time.
facts.quote: Its teeth were continually replacing and packed into dental batteries that contained hundreds of teeth, only a relative handful of which were in use at any time.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus fed on vegetation ranging from the ground up to approximately 4 meters (13 feet) above.
facts.quote: Feeding would have been from the ground up to ~4 meters (13 ft) above.

facts.statement: The genus Kritosaurus was named by Brown in 1910.
facts.quote: genus_authority: Brown, 1910

facts.statement: The species Kritosaurus navajovius was named by Brown in 1910.
facts.quote: species_authority: Brown, 1910

facts.statement: The name Kritosaurus is sometimes misinterpreted as "noble lizard," referring to a presumed Roman noble profile found in the nasal region fragments.
facts.quote: Su nombre es malinterpretado a veces como "lagarto noble", en referencia la presunta "nariz aguileña" que se relaciona con los nobles romanos del perfil de la región nasal que se encontró en fragmentos, y desarticulada siendo restaurada originalmente como plana.

facts.statement: The taxonomy of Kritosaurus is complicated by its historical association with Gryposaurus, Anasazisaurus, and Naashoibitosaurus, and remains unresolved until better remains are described.
facts.quote: Su taxonomía se ve envuelta en una complicada historia donde también se incluyen a Gryposaurus, Anasazisaurus, y Naashoibitosaurus. Este enredo seguirá estando sin resolver hasta que mejores restos de Kritosaurus sean descritos.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus had a special adaptation in its snout that resulted in a wide tip.
facts.quote: Kritosaurus presentaba una adaptación especial en el hocico, que resultaba ancho en su extremo.

facts.statement: Kritosaurus walked on both two and four legs.
facts.quote: Caminaba sobre tanto en dos como en cuatro patas

facts.statement: Kritosaurus had a narrow head with a bump on the crown containing air passages that allowed it to make sounds.
facts.quote: su cabeza era estrecha con un bulto en la corona, con conductos por los que pasaba aire y le permitía emitir sonidos con él

facts.statement: The type species Kritosaurus navajovius was 10 meters long and weighed around 4 tons.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, K. navajovius, tenía una longitud de 10 metros y un peso de alrededor de 4 toneladas

facts.statement: A reconstruction from the early 2000s using additional skull fragments shows a crest in front of the eyes.
facts.quote: una reconstrucción de principios de los años 2000 que usa material adicional de fragmentos del cráneo que no había sido colocado antes muestran una cresta delante de los ojos

facts.statement: The skull length is estimated at 87 centimeters from the top of the beak where the square articulates with the lower jaw at the back of the skull.
facts.quote: La longitud del cráneo se estima en 87 centímetros desde el pico superior en donde el cuadrado articula con la mandíbula inferior en la parte posterior del cráneo

facts.statement: Potential diagnostic features of Kritosaurus include a predentary without dentate crenulation, a sustained downward curve at the lower beak insertion, and a heavy, somewhat rectangular maxilla.
facts.quote: Potenciales características de diagnóstico de Kritosaurus incluye un predentario sin la crenulación dentada, una curva hacia abajo sostenida en la inserción del pico inferior, y un pesado, algo rectangular maxilar

facts.statement: According to Prieto-Márquez's 2013 rediagnosis, Kritosaurus is distinguished by an extensive dorsolateral maxillary margin, a jugal with an orbital constriction deeper than the infratemporal, an infratemporal fenestra larger than the orbit with a dorsal margin elevated above the dorsal orbital margin in adults, the frontal bone participating in the orbital margin, and paired caudal parasagittal processes of the nasals resting on the frontal bones.
facts.quote: Según Prieto-Márquez, quien volvió a diagnosticar este género en 2013, Kritosaurus se puede distinguir en función de las siguientes características: la longitud del margen dorsolateral del maxilar es extensa, el yugal presenta una constricción orbitaria que es más profunda que la infratemporal, la fenestra infratemporal es mayor que la órbita y tiene un margen dorsal que está muy elevado por encima del margen orbitario dorsal en adultos, el hueso frontal participa en el margen orbital, la presencia de procesos parasagitales caudales pareados de las nasales que descansan sobre los huesos frontales

facts.statement: Kritosaurus is definitively known only from a partial skull, lower jaws, and associated undescribed postcranial material.
facts.quote: Kritosaurus es solamente definitivamente determinado de un cráneo parcial y mandíbulas inferiores, y de material asociado postcraneal sin describir

facts.statement: Kritosaurus lived from the Santonian to the Maastrichtian, between 85.7 and 66 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Santonian to Maastrichtian (85.7 to 66 million years ago)

facts.statement: Kritosaurus belongs to the parent group Kritosaurini.
facts.quote: Parent group: Kritosaurini

facts.statement: Kritosaurus is classified in the family Hadrosauridae.
facts.quote: Family: Hadrosauridae

facts.statement: Kritosaurus belongs to the class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia
